RE: MOTION FOR SUSPENSION OF THE QUESTION HOUR 
SHRI JIBON ROY (West Bengal): Sir, I have given to you a motion for the 
suspension of Question Hour. Five lakh people, representing several sections 
of the masses all over the country, have come to Delhi with their demands and 
they are demonstrating before Parliament. They say that a kind of jobless growth 
is taking place in our country. T he level of employment is going down and 
rural poverty has increased. The people are astounded with the announcement 
of the Finance Minister that all the public sector undertakings' share will be 
reduced to 26 per cent. The people are shocked at this annou ncement. Sir, the 
Government has taken up the policy of liberalisation... 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Please sit down. 
SHRI JIBON ROY: Sir, the Government may have a sound liberalisation 
policy, but if that policy is not followed by the introduction of land reforms... 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Mr. Jibon Roy, I am not allowing any suspension of 
the Question Hour. During Question Hour, nothing else but questions are taken 
up. 
SHRI JIBON ROY: Sir, this is the genuine demand of the masses. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: I am not objecting to their demands. I am only saying 
that the Question Hour will not be suspended. Inviolability of the Question 
Hour is the unanimous decision of the House. The hon. Members should not go 
against their own decision.

WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS 
National policy for food processing industries 
†*202.  DR.D.MASTHAN: 
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER SINGH: 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a national policy is required to be formulated 
for expansion and development of food processing industries in the country; 
† Original notice of the Question was received in Hindi. 
7 

RAJYA SABHA [9 March, 2000] 
(b) if so, whether Government have given any preliminary consideration 
for formulation of such policy; and 
(c) if so, what priorities have been set for policy formulation and by when 
it would be finalised? 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI SUNDER LAL PATWA): (a) 
Yes, Sir. 
(b) and (c) The task of formulation of F ood Processing Policy is under 
way. Broadly, the Food Processing Policy would cover issues relating to 
availability of raw material, backward linkages, processing facilities 
including post -harvest infrastructure, packaging food quality and safety, 
marketing of products —domestic and export, awareness about processed 
food and fiscal incentives. 
As wide ranging consultations would be required with the State 
Governments and other inter -related departments of Government of India 
before the policy is announced, i t is difficult to indicate a timeframe within 
which the policy will be finalised. 
*203. [Postponed] 
Survival of Small Scale Industries 
*204.     SHRI GAYA SINGH: 
SHRI J. CHITHARANJAN:  
Will the Minister of SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES AND AGRO 
AND RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Small Scale Industries (SSIs) will not be 
able to survive when India will be totally free from the Quota Restrictions 
(QRs) after April, 2001; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) how Government plan to face such a situation? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY (SHRI OMAR ABDULLAH): (a) and (b) The Small Scale Industries 
in India have enough resilience to withstand the impact of phasing out of 
Quantitative Restrictions beyond April,  2001 as is evident from their recent 
track record. 
(c) The Government has put in place several measures to help our small 
enterprises become globally competitive. These include special focus on areas 
8 

[9 March, 2000] RAJYA SABHA 
such as technology upgra dation, infrastructure assistance through cluster 
approach, timely availability of credit, adoption of modern management 
practices, use of electronic infrastructure and other IT applications, marketing 
and timely information dissemination, including sensitisation of small industries

Most Favoured Nation Status to Pakistan 
*210. SHRI V.N. GADGIL: Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government believe that Pakistan should be declared as a 
terrorist state; 
(b) if so, why is Pakistan still accorded a Most Favoured Nation status 
despite no reciprocity; 
(c) why has not the liberal visa regime for Pakistani visitors been 
terminated when its blatant misuse is well known; and 
(d) what efforts have been made to have it declared as a terrorist state? 
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI JASWANT SINGH): 
(a) to (d) The facts regarding Pakistan's state sponsorship of terrorism in Jammu 
and Kashmir and elsewhere in India have been effectively and appropriately 
brought before several international fora and have also been raised at high -
level bilateral discussions with world leaders. The international community 
now openly recognises Pakistan's state sponsorship of terrorism and the impact 
this has on the security of the country and the region. 
Contrary to its commitment under the WTO, Pakistan has not extended 
MFN treatment to India. While Government continue to meet its international 
trade obligations under its WTO commitments, they also continue to take all 
necessary actions to protect the country's trade interests vis-a-vis Pakistan. 
Government is of the view that the promotion of people-to-people contacts 
between India and Pakistan contributes to its desire of establishing a relationship 
of peace, friendship and cooperation with that country. While pursuing such an 
approach, Government exercises due vigilance including in its visa policy for 
Pakistani nationals so that the security of the country is safeguarded.

Statement 
The Government of India has set up the Ministry of Information 
Technology on 15.10.1999 to facilitate all initiatives in the IT sector including 
Internet, e-commerce, IT education and IT based education. 
18 

[9 March, 2000] RAJYA SABHA 
The Government has accepted the first report of the National IT Task 
Force outlining 108 recommendations of the IT Action Plan. These 
recommendations suggest measures and policies covering a wide spectrum. of 
issues relating to telecommunication, finance banking, revenue, commerce, 
electronics, HRD, defence and rural development to enable India to emerge as 
an Information Technology super power within the next ten years. A target of 
software export of US$50 billion by the year 2008 has been set. The Task Force 
has also recommended a goal of ""IT for AH" by 2008 in India. The second and 
third report of the Task Force address the . issues and strategy for development 
of hardware industry, R&D in the area of IT, manpower training and education. 
All Government Departments are required to spend 2 -3% of their 
budget towards implementation of IT. To induce more investment in R&D in 
computers, a weighted deduction of 125% on the sums paid to any 
university, college or institution or a scientific research association for the 
purpose of scientific, social or statistical research has been provided. 
Many States of India have drawn up comprehensive IT plans and have 
come out with IT policies which will help in creating a conducive 
environment for high growth of high-tech industries. 
Government of India has also formed a Rs. 100 crores National Venture 
Capital Fund in association with the Small Industries Development Bank of 
India (SIDBI), Industrial Dev elopment Bank of India (IDBI) for the IT 
industry particularly for small and medium enterprises. 
Penetration of Personnel Computers (PC) in the country at present is 
slightly more than 3 per 1000 persons. The target is to increase the PC 
penetration to 20 per 1000 person by the year 2008. To push the demand of 
PCs in the country, depreciation on computers has been increased to 60%. 
Government has implemented Internet Service providers (ISPs) Policy, 
ISPs are allowed to set up International Gateways and hire  bandwidth on 
foreign satellites. Public and private sectors have been licensed to provide 
internet services in the country. No licence fee is payable for first five years 
and a nominal fee of one rupee is to be paid after five years. The internet 
policy approved by Governments provides inter -connection of networks and 
setting up of international gateway by the internet service provider 
independent of VSNL. The infrastructure for Internet is proposed to be 
19 

RAJYA SABHA [9 March, 2000] 
upgraded as below: 
(a) Department of Telecom Services (DTS) is setting up national internet 
backbone in the country. 
(b) Internet Service Providers are allowed to set up last mile linkages 
freely by fibre optic or by radio communication. 
(c) The Internet access is also allowed through authorized cable TV. 
The tariff for internet access has been recently reduced. DTS have recently 
offered 20% concession on rental for leased lines taken and used for internet 
applications. Students are being given one time concession on internet accounts 
by DTS. Access to internet on local call basis from the nearest internet node has 
been provided throughout the country except in Andaman and Nicobar Island 
and Leh (J and K). The existing departmental Public Gall Operators (PCO) and 
Subscriber Trunk Dailing (STD) booths are proposed to be upgraded to public 
tele-info/cyber centres. These centres will provide multi -utility services such 
as internet, e-mail access and internet libraries. 
To provide the legal framework for transaction on Internet and e-commerce, 
Information Technology Bill, 1999 was introduced in the last session of the 
Parliament. Such a legal framework will facilitate and give a fillip to the e -
commerce activities in the country.

Involving Youth in Planning Process 
*218. SHRI KARTAR SINGH DUGGAL: Will the PRIME MINISTER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether any steps are being taken to involve the youth in planning 
process as the Late Prime Minister, Jawahar Lal Nehru, the harbinger of the 
concept of Planning in India considered people's participation as the prime 
sanction being national planning; 
(b) whether there is any scheme to revive Planning Fora in the universities 
and colleges which were higher active at one time; and 
(c) what is the component of the outfit in the Planning Commission to 
ensure integrated publicity to the planning activity? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING, 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME 
IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF 
ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC GRIEVANCES OF THE 
MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRI 
ARUN SHOURIE): (a) Yes, Sir. The involvement of youth in the Planning Process 
is being operationalised through various programmes of Youth Affairs under 
the Department of Youth Affairs and Sports by providing them chance of 
community service and awareness about various social issues etc. Among these 
programmes, National Service Scheme (NSS), Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan 
(NYKS), National Service Volunteer Scheme (NSVS), Assistance to Voluntary 
Organisations in the field of youth and Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of 
Youth Development are important one. 
The brief of some of the programmes is given below:—  
National Service Scheme: National Service Scheme is one of the major 
student youth programme started in 1969 aimed at development of student 
personality through voluntary participation in community service. During 
25 

RAJYA SABHA [9 March, 2000] 
1998-99 NSS had about 15 lakh student volunteers on its roll spread over 189 
universities and senior secondary schools. From its inception, more than 1.52 
crore students from the universities, colleges and institutions of higher learning 
have been benefitted from NSS activities. Due to its overwhelming popularity 
and demand, the scheme has been extended to the students of 2 level in selected 
institutions. It has two types of programmes viz. "Regular Activities" and 
"Special Camping Programme". Regular activities include constructive work 
in adopted villages and slums, blood donation, adult and non-formal education, 
health, nutrition, family welfare, AIDS awareness campaigns, tree plantation 
etc. Under 'Special Camping Programe' a camp of 10 days duration is conducted 
every year in the adopted areas on a specific theme "Youth for Rural 
Reconstruction", "Youth for Special Harmony" etc. 
Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan: It has its district offices in about 500 
districts of the country. Over the year NYKS has become the largest grass routs 
level organisation in Asia-pacific region, catering to the needs of more than 6.4 
million rural female and male youth enrolled through 1.79 lakh village -based 
organisations, named Youth Clubs in the areas covering education, training, 
health awareness, self-employment, financial assistance. Besides this, awareness 
generation and activities for the overall development of the rural communities 
are also being taken in the villages with emphasis on value, vision and voluntary 
action. NYKS has also taken programmes in collaboration with other agencies 
like ""Youth action goal-2000" in U.P. in collaboration with other agencies like 
"Youth action goal-2000" in U.P. in collaboration with UNICEF, Awareness on 
Child Rights and Youth Against AIDS Campaign in the North- Eastern States 
etc. NYKS also organises work camps also involving youth club memebrs in 
project planning and management and to improve the organisational skills of 
youth club memebrs. 
Assistance to Voluntary Organisations in the fields of Youth: The main 
focus of this scheme has been on vocational training programmes to promote 
self-employment of youth. Assistance is also being given for conducting youth 
leadership training program me to promote cadres of young dynamic persons 
who would act as catalysts of social change in the rural areas. 
(b) No, Sir. At present, there is no scheme to revive Planning Forum in the 
Universities and Colleges. 
26 

[9 March, 2000] RAJYA SABHA

open border for staging anti -India activities, the concerned agencies of His 
Majesty's Government of Nepal and the Government of India remain in regular 
touch, both directly and through bilateral institutional mechanism, such as the 
Joint Working Group on Border Management and Home Secretary level talks. 
Concrete measures and cooperation on security issues are discussed, reviewed 
and followed up at these meetings. SeveraLmeasures have been taken to enhance 
cooperation with Nepal, particularly with regard to implementing effective 
border management. Efforts have been made by both sides to jointly coordinate 
measures, including stepping up vigil along the contiguous border districts of 
India and Nepal, to prevent misuse of the open India-Nepal border for activities 
directed against India. On their part, His Majesty's Government of Nepal have 
assured that their territory would not be used for activities inimical to India's 
interest and have been extending their cooperation to the Government of India

1571.    SHRI CM. IBRAHIM: 
SHRI EDUARDO FALERIO: 
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
78 

[9 March,2000] RAJYA SABHA 
(a) whether Government have sought clarifications from the US and other 
principal signatories to CTBT as to how far signing of CTBT is compatible 
with maintenance of Nuclear deterrent by the signatories, if so, with what 
response; 
(b) what are the main reasons for refusal of the US Congress to ratify the 
CTBT; 
 
(c) whether Government have since taken any steps to bring about 
consensus about signing of CTBT amongst different sections of Parliament; 
and 
(d) if so, whether any of the parties have sought clarifications and if so the 
details thereof and the Government's response thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI AJITKUMAR PANJA); (a) The Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty 
(CTBT) only prohibits underground explosive nuclear testing; other activities 
relating to development, non -explosive testing, production and s afe 
maintenance of nuclear arsenals are not restricted. Thus the CTBT is entirely 
compatible with the maintenance of a nuclear deterrent by those States which 
have already conducted nuclear tests. The Government's view in this regard is 
shared by the US. 
(b) The two main reservations expressed by the US senators voting against 
the CTBT related to lack of trust in maintaining the integrity of the US nuclear 
weapons stockpile without further explosive testing and doubts regarding the 
verifiability of the Treaty. 
(c) and (d) India's stand on the CTBT was articulated by the Prime Minister 
in the UN General Assembly in September 1998 and in Parliament in December 
1998. This was reiterated by the External Affairs Minister at the UN General 
Assembly in September 1999. The priority of our meeting the country's national 
security concerns having been addressed, the Government believes that we 
now need to convey reassurance to the international community and, in this 
regard, desires to develop a national consensus. The Government is encouraged 
by the constructive response to its efforts to build a consensus on the issue of 
CTBT and intends to pursue this exercise.

Action against corrupt public servants 
1604. SHRI ABANI ROY: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether CVC has been considering to nab corrupt public servants and 
making them liable for prosecution even after retirement; 
(b) if so, whether vigilance officers have been deputed to arrange traps to 
nab the corrupt public servants; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) other stringent steps Government propose to take to ensure that  
Government servants may not indulge into unfair means to earn money? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF PERSONNEL 
AND TRAINING AND DEPARTMENT OF PENSION AND PENSIONERS' 
WELFARE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND 
PENSIONS (SHRIMATI VASUNDHRA RAJE):  (a) to (c) A public servant 
continues to be liable for any acts of omission or commission committed by 
him while in service even after his retirement, under the provisions of Prevention 
of Corruption Act, 1988. However, under that Act, traps can be arranged to nab 
the corrupt public servant(s) only by Police Officers. The Prevention of 
Corruption Act does not empower the Vigilance Officers to arrange such traps. 
(d) The punitive actions being taken under the Prevention of Corruption 
Act, 1988 duly supporte d by various Conduct Rules governing the service 
conditions of public servants act as a deterrent against corruption. Moreover, 
the drive against corruption in public services to check malpractices in 
administration and to provide efficient public services is a continuing process. 
The policies formulated in this regard are modified from time to time in order to 
make them more effective and responsive to the changing environment. Some 
of the steps taken by the Government in this regard are as under:— 
1. Spec ial drives are launched by the Central Bureau of Investigation 
from time to time to detect cases of disproportionate assets, to organise 
traps to apprehend public servants while demanding and accepting 
illegal gratification and conduct surprise check at sensitive places. 
109 

 
RAJYA SABHA [9 March, 2000] 
2. The Central Vigilance Commission Bill has been introduced in the Lok 
Sabha on 20.12.1999 to confer statutory status on the CVC. The Bill stands 
referred to the Joint Committee of both the Houses of Parliame nt on 
21.12.1999 for consideration and its recommendations. 
3. The Central Vigilance Commission has been vested powers vide Para 3(v) of 
Department of Personnel and Training Resolution No. 371/20/ 99-AVD. III 
dated 4th April, 1999 to exercise superintendence over the vigilance 
administration. The Commission has issued several instructions to reduce 
the scope of corruption such as creating a culture of honesty, greater 
transparency in administration, electronics clearance system and 
computerisation of banks, sensitising the public etc. The Central Vigilance 
Commission has also issued Special Chapters on vigilance management in 
public sector banks and public sector undertakings. 
4. It is proposed to set up the institution of Lok Pal to look into the allegations 
of corruption against high public functionaries. Lok Pal Bill was introduced 
in the Lok Sabha on 3.8.1998 but lapsed on the dissolution of the 12th Lok 
Sabha on 26.4.1999. Steps are being taken to introduce the Bill afresh. 
5. The Government set up a Working Group on 'Right to Information and 
Transparency' in January, 1997 which submitted its report to the 
Government on 21st May, 1997. The report of the Group has been processed 
and a Bill for Freedom of Information has been drafted. The Bill is presently 
under examination for introduction in the Parliament. 
6. Recognising that an important aspect of Preventive Vigilance is to ensure 
transparency in public administration, measures of administrative 
reforms such as introduction of Citizens Charters and setting up of 
Facilitation Centre have been initiated. The review and simplification of 
laws, rules and procedures has also been taken up.

1645. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR: Will the PR IME MINISTER be

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING. 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS AND 
PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC 
GRIEVANCES OFTHE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND 
PENSIONS (SHRI ARUN SHOURIE): (a) and (b) No, Sir. In fact, the North-Eastern 
States have achieved higher literacy rate and lower crude birth/death rate and infant 
morality rate than the All-India average. However, the growth in per-capita Net State 
Domestic Product (NSDP) at constant prices (1980-81) of these States during the 
period 1992-93 to 1996-97 ranged between 1.63% (Assam) and 7.19% (Tripura), 
as compared to 5.33% recorded at the national level. The major factors contributing 
to the slow growth in per-capita. income in these States are: 
(i) Higher level of administrative cost. 
(ii) Poor resource base. 
(iii) Increasing security related expenditure. 
(iv) Under-utilization of funds available under the Centrally Sponsored 
Schemes owing to inadequate provision in Annual Plans to meet 
the States' shares. 
144 

[9 March, 2000] RAJYA SABHA 
(v) Low level of investment in the industrial Sector. 
To ensure speedy economic development of the Region, several steps 
have been taken to augment the development assistance from the Centre, which 
include: 
(i) 0% of Normal Central Assistance is earmarked for Special Category 
States, which include N.E. States. 
(ii) 90% of Plan assistance is grant and 10% loan as against 30% grant 
and 70% loan for other States. 
(iii) State's contribution of 15% which is mandatory for the Basic Minimum 
Services schemes, is not applicable to N.E. States. 
(iv) 10% of Plan provision of the Central Ministries/Departments has been 
earmarked for development of N.E. States. 
(v) Over and above the State Plan outlays, which have been increasing 
over the years, funds are also being sanctioned out of the Non-Lapsable 
Central Pool of Resources created through transfer of unspent balance 
of the earmarked outlays of the Central Ministries and Departments 
meant for development of the N.E. States. 
(vi) The North Eastern Council is also engaged in the development of 
infrastructure in the Region. 
(vii) Special dispensation has been made in respect of the Accelerated 
Irrigation Benefit Programme (AIBP) by incorporating minor irrigation 
projects for the North-Eastern States and allowing 25% of the State's 
share, as against 33% for others, in availing of Central Loan Assistance. 
(viii) Diversion to the extent of 20% of the Normal Central Assistance (Plan) 
is allowed for Non-Plan purposes. 
(ix) Sensitizing States on the need for reducing the non-plan expenditure.
